props.title: Wish Upon a Star

sections.content: **Wish Upon a Star** (1996) belongs to the golden age of Disney Channel and ABC Family original movies that dominated teen programming in the mid-1990s. Starring Katherine Heigl in one of her earliest roles, this body-swap comedy follows sisters who magically switch places after wishing on a shooting star. It's a direct descendant of classic switch films like Freaky Friday (1976) and Vice Versa (1988), but with a sisterly twist that allows it to explore teenage social dynamics and family relationships of the 90s.

sections.content: The film taps into the rich tradition of magical transformation stories that dominated family entertainment in the 1990s. Like Teen Witch (1989) and Life-Size (2000), it uses supernatural elements to explore coming-of-age themes and sibling dynamics. The film's portrayal of high school social hierarchies and sister relationships feels particularly authentic for its era, predating similar themes in **She's All That** (1999) and **10 Things I Hate About You** (1999).

What sets **Wish Upon a Star** (1996) apart is its focus on sisterly bonds rather than parent-child relationships that were common in other body-swap films. Katherine Heigl's performance as both the studious older sister and the popular younger sister showcases her early talent, presaging her later success in films like **27 Dresses** (2008) and **Knocked Up** (2007). sections.content: The film exists in a specific moment of teen-focused magical realism that included hits like **Now and Then** (1995) and **Casper** (1995). These films merged supernatural elements with grounded coming-of-age stories, creating a unique subgenre that influenced later works like **The Princess Diaries** (2001) and **A Cinderella Story** (2004).
